I will keep most of my land in the wheat-maize rotation because that is the steadiest way for me to use my 10.1 mu, my well irrigation, and my family labor. Since some people in my household work off-farm, I will not make the plan too labor-heavy. I will put 8.0 mu into winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land, and I will keep 2.1 mu in cotton because I already grow it and it helps me spread risk across crops. For wheat, I will use improved seed, put enough fertilizer on early, irrigate three times with my well, and aim for a stable grain yield. For maize, I will use hybrid seed because I care most about dependable output on the summer crop, keep irrigation moderate, and use simpler field management after wheat harvest. For cotton, I will keep a smaller area because it takes more field watching and more spraying, but I will still grow it because it gives me another source of income. I will use practical input levels that I believe I can afford and manage myself, and I will focus on steady production rather than chasing the highest possible yield.
